newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina cuts welfare rolls 24 pct in two years.
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina cuts welfare rolls 24 pct in two years.

text.p: North Carolina has trimmed its welfare rolls by 24 percent since the state began its welfare-to-work program two years ago, Gov. Jim Hunt said.
The reduction has saved the state $112.4 million in welfare costs, Hunt said Monday in a conference at Baptist Hospital in Winston-Salem.
North Carolina had 86,267 families receiving welfare as of June 1, down from 113,485 in June 1995, before the program began.
The program requires welfare recipients to get a job or enroll in a job training course within 12 weeks of receiving their first check, and limits benefits to two years in most cases.

Recipients must sign contracts describing how they plan to become self-sufficient. Since the program began, 38,700 families have found jobs and stayed off the welfare rolls. Since July 1996, 9,450 have had their benefits cut for failing to meet terms of the contracts.
